title: Nepal v. State of U.P. and others
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Surya Prakash Kesarwani, J.; Jayant Banerji, J.
disposition: Writ disposed of; petitioner relegated to paragraph 6.8 objection.
headnote: A writ challenging a recovery citation is disposed of without opinion on merits, with liberty to file an objection under paragraph 6.8 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 before respondent No. 4 within three weeks, to be decided by a reasoned speaking order within four weeks after hearing.
facts: Nepal filed a writ in the Allahabad High Court challenging a recovery citation. The petition was adjourned on 17 December 2021. On 7 April 2022 none appeared for the petitioner. Counsel for respondent Nos. 2 and 4 stated on instructions that the petitioner could object to the citation before respondent No. 4 under paragraph 6.8 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, and that any such objection would be decided in accordance with law within a time-bound period.

holding_units.topic: objection to recovery citation as alternate remedy
holding_units.holding: Without expressing any opinion on the merits, the writ petition challenging the recovery citation is disposed of with liberty to the petitioner to submit an objection before respondent No. 4 under paragraph 6.8 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 within three weeks; if so submitted, respondent No. 4 shall decide it by a reasoned and speaking order within the next four weeks after affording a reasonable opportunity of hearing.

principle_tags.application: The Court disposed of the writ without examining the recovery citation on merits and relegated the consumer to the statutory objection under paragraph 6.8 before respondent No. 4, with a time-bound speaking-order direction.
Counsel's statement that an objection under paragraph 6.8 lay against the impugned recovery citation was accepted as the appropriate statutory course in place of writ adjudication.

not_decided.point: merits of the challenge to the recovery citation
not_decided.note: The Court expressly declined to express any opinion on the merits.
